Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Charles Baudelaire (author, Wikidata Q501), died 1867; Guillaume Apollinaire (notes, Wikidata Q133855), died 1918. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Baudelaire, Charles, 1821-1867; Apollinaire, Guillaume, 1880-1918 [Commentator]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: Les fleurs du mal, Paris : Librairie des bibliophiles parisiens, 1917, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/lesfleursdl00baud. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 91%, 85%, 96% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Guillaume Apollinaire, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
